💡 COUNTER LEARNED — a moth the size of a dinner plate, catching light wrong: Hit it while it folds. The Wing Flash only fires FORWARD — it must face you. Circle while it folds its wings and hit it before the wings open. It can't flash what's behind it. (Someone at the haven knew the trick.)

A man, maybe 40s, with a long braid has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. A woman, maybe 30s, with deep-set eyes drew a low feathery plant with tiny flat pods in the dirt for the others. It'll wash away. The knowledge won't.

Rasha spends the afternoon with the tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Raw, it knots the stomach. Cooked... fine. The fire learns the rule before the name: cook it, or else.
★ IDENTIFIED: White Oak Acorns. White oak acorn. Lobed leaves, sweet acorns. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 White Oak Acorns. The tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps you've been looking at for days finally has a name, and now you'll never unsee it.

Devon has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Rasha drew a vine with elaborate purple-and-white flowers and egg-sized green fruit that wrinkles yellow when ripe in the dirt for the others. It'll wash away. The knowledge won't.

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — ducks in a row: Break the line. The line is one animal, but only while it's whole. Strike a duck that ISN'T the head and the line splits — both halves hunt on their own and the formation dies. Break the line, then thin the pieces. (Someone at the haven knew the trick.)
